title: House of Luxembourg
capsule: The House of Luxembourg rose from the County of Luxembourg - held by Count Henry V from 1247 through his mother Ermesinde and descended from the House of Limburg-Arlon - to the summit of European power when Henry VII was elected King of the Romans in 1308 and crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 1312. The dynasty secured Bohemia through John the Blind's marriage to the Premyslid heiress Elisabeth in 1310, and reached its height under Charles IV (r. 1346-1378), who issued the Golden Bull of 1356 - the enduring constitutional framework of the Empire - and acquired Brandenburg in 1373. Around the close of this period the house faced setbacks, including the deposition of King Wenceslaus by the prince-electors in 1400, before Sigismund consolidated its fortunes from 1410.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial holdings of the Luxembourg dynasty are well documented through imperial charters and coronation records; the map footprint here represents the County of Luxembourg proper rather than the full extent of dynastic rule over Bohemia, Brandenburg, and the Empire.
